samples.summary: Header/footer fix is only applied to the caret-only branch of `forEachBlockInSelection`; the top-level multi-block branch still walks `doc.document.blocks` while indexing with the context-aware `doc.getBlockIndex()`
samples.evidence: The delta changes `siblingsOf()` (text-editor.ts:2865) to `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` precisely because "the caret can sit in a header/footer list, whose blocks live outside the body array". But the sibling walker's multi-block branch still does `const startIdx = this.doc.getBlockIndex(range.anchor.blockId)` (2831) / `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks` (2836) and then `fn(topLevel[i], topLevel)`. `Doc.getBlockIndex` resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:271-273), so with a multi-block selection inside a header/footer the indices are header-relative but the array is the body — Tab/Cmd+] plans levels for the wrong blocks (or dereferences `undefined` when the header has more blocks than the body), i.e. the header-list outcome this delta claims is unmet for selections and can mis-mutate body content. Note editor.ts's sibling walker (editor.ts:1689) already uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` here, so the two parallel implementations of the same walker now disagree.

samples.summary: Design doc's list-level section describes sibling containers only as "different table cells"; the delta extends the rule to header/footer context blocks without recording it
samples.evidence: docs.md §"Changing a list level carries the subtree" (lines 148-158) says the walker "hands each covered block together with the sibling array containing it, so blocks in different table cells are planned as separate list contexts". The delta makes header/footer regions a third sibling container (`getContextBlocks()`), and adds a repaint requirement (children outside the selection must be marked dirty). Neither is captured in the canonical doc or the active task note (docs/tasks/active/20260908-docs-list-level-subtree-todo.md), so the documented shape now under-describes the behavior. Cost stays inside the codebase.

samples.summary: `markDirty` bookkeeping placed inside the per-change loop and resolved against the body-only `layout.blockParentMap`
samples.evidence: applyListLevelChanges resolves `layout.blockParentMap.get(change.block.id)` per change; that map is the body layout's map (the merged header/footer map is only pushed into `doc.setBlockParentMap`, editor.ts:1573-1580), so in header/footer context the lookup always misses and the raw block id is marked. It happens to be harmless because header/footer layouts are recomputed unconditionally each render, but the invalidation concern is arguably the render layer's, not this planner's — one dirty-marking pass after the write loop would express it once.

verdict.reason: Verified in-tree. text-editor.ts:2831-2836 computes selection bounds with `this.doc.getBlockIndex(...)`, which resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:271-273 -> 158-162, returning header/footer blocks when `editContext !== 'body'`), yet walks `this.doc.document.blocks` and passes it as the siblings array (2838-2850). Only the caret-only fallback (2855-2856 via siblingsOf, 2863-2873) is context-aware, matching the reviewer's description exactly. Nothing guards this: `doc.editContext` is synced at 403-406, and Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ (1120-1122, 1306-1315) reach applyListLevelChanges -> forEachBlockInSelection (2712-2716) with no editContext check; multi-block header/footer selections are a supported state, as deleteSelection's dedicated header/footer multi-block path shows (3767-3789, which correctly uses getContextBlocks). editor.ts:1684-1702 implements the same walker over `doc.getContextBlocks()`, so the two parallel walkers now give different answers for the same gesture — duplicated logic that diverges, with a user-visible consequence (list-level gesture in a header/footer plans levels against body blocks). No refutation ground applies.
